evidence.exact_quote: Concern is a first-class durable record distinct from review finding, annotation, blocked episode, and graph patch request. The visible concern contract carries `concern_id`, `project_id`, run refs, scope refs, evidence refs, source refs, lineage refs, severity, category, status, and governance metadata.

These surfaces share one escalation ladder across Orchestrator, Dashboard, thread badges, and notifications. `attention_required` remains distinct from `blocked`, and persistent blockers resurface on meaningful change or persistence even when advisory warnings are quieted.

items.impact: Builders have a stable durable concern identity and a shared escalation projection instead of surface-local warning records.
items.statement: The concern and escalation model explicitly separates durable concern identity, blocked state, severity, operational blocking effect, owners, and mirrored consumers.
items.title: Concern identity and shared escalation are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime alert lifecycle defines `/auto-resolution`: an alert may auto-resolve on healthy refresh, downgrade to historical `/seen` after acknowledgment, and clear badges consistently across mirrored surfaces.
Repeated sightings with the same root cause update the existing attention thread, while interruptive notification surfaces fire again only when severity or state changes.

When mirrored surfaces disagree, each issue class declares freshness/authority order (`/authority`). Secondary surfaces with older data say `updating` or `state may be outdated` instead of presenting conflicting definitive copy.

items.impact: A stale healthy refresh or out-of-order repeated sighting can clear or downgrade a still-active incident, with mirrored badges disagreeing and no falsifiable reconciliation rule.
items.statement: The alert lifecycle names auto-resolution, coalescing, and authority ordering but does not define freshness bounds, event ordering, idempotency, or the proof required before an active alert may clear.
items.title: Alert auto-resolution lacks race-safe proof

- queued messages are FIFO with max 2 entries, transient, and not restart-persisted
- tool approval dialogs launched from Chat must preserve thread context and return focus to the composer after completion

items.statement: Chat specifies virtualized stable-identity message rows, bounded transient FIFO queueing, owner-routed activity detail, and approval focus restoration.

segments.summary: Reviewed concern and alert lifecycle, owner routing, bulk actions, route anchors, chat, File Manager, editor and annotation surfaces, activity and runtime panes, widgets, and state flow. Exact contracts are strong, but alert reconciliation and project-state merge semantics remain high-risk gaps.

Reviewed persistence boundaries, context and Agent-Config projections, confirmation, undo, loading/error/blocked patterns, event refresh, approvals, clipboard, LSP affordances, anti-flicker, terminal throttling, responsive layouts, and accessibility. Projection truth is explicit; scroll anchoring, overload handling, responsive edge cases, and accessibility verification are not closed.

Reviewed Slint/Rust organization, view lifecycle and virtualization, redb key families, authority mapping, startup restore, terminal and dev-session recovery, chat recovery, migration mapping, clipboard gate, and early risk inventory. Ownership and liveness truth are strong; browser-profile privacy, partial restore, and destructive message rewrite behavior are material gaps.

Reviewed the full risk table, promoted-feature closure, cross-reference and locked-decision appendices, Dashboard widget grid/catalog and migration, Persona editing/runtime disclosure/mappings, and rendering-surface inventory. Persona disclosure and capture send-gating are explicit; engine wording, archive lifecycle, widget eligibility, and Persona precedence remain ambiguous.

Reviewed browser automation, capture, hosting, platform, performance and acceptance behavior; Plan/Deep Plan, TODO, annotations and Wizard handoff; compatibility scheduler/recovery lineage; and canonical blocked/recovery behavior. Major gaps remain in authenticated browser authority, bundled-runtime operations, plan approval versioning, imported-context lifecycle, and blocked-action execution semantics.

Where are browser profile encryption, cookie and localStorage retention, purge, export, and project-deletion semantics canonicalized?

Where are allowed_action_ids versioning, actor authority, idempotency, in-flight state, and partial-failure reconciliation defined for blocked episodes?
What host-by-widget eligibility matrix reconciles the four-entry Dashboard catalog with the broader Widget_System page-widget catalog?
